The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

import pandas as pd
import lightgbm as lgb
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
import numpy as np

# Load data
train = pd.read_csv('/app/data/train.csv')
val = pd.read_csv('/app/data/val.csv')
test = pd.read_csv('/app/data/test.csv')

# Identify columns
num_cols = [c for c in train.columns if c.startswith('num_')]
bin_cols = [c for c in train.columns if c.startswith('bin_')]
cat_cols = [c for c in train.columns if c.startswith('cat_')]

# Target
y_train = train['target']
y_val = val['target']

# Features
X_train = train[num_cols + bin_cols + cat_cols]
X_val = val[num_cols + bin_cols + cat_cols]
X_test = test[num_cols + bin_cols + cat_cols]

# Convert categorical columns to 'category' dtype for LightGBM
for col in cat_cols:
    X_train[col] = X_train[col].astype('category')
    X_val[col] = X_val[col].astype('category')
    X_test[col] = X_test[col].astype('category')

# Initialize and train LightGBM model
model = lgb.LGBMClassifier(
    n_estimators=1000,
    learning_rate=0.05,
    num_leaves=31,
    objective='binary',
    metric='auc',
    random_state=42,
    n_jobs=-1
)

model.fit(
    X_train, y_train,
    eval_set=[(X_val, y_val)],
    callbacks=[lgb.early_stopping(stopping_rounds=50)]
)

# Predict probabilities for the positive class
y_pred = model.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]

# Save predictions to CSV
pred_df = pd.DataFrame({'target': y_pred})
pred_df.to_csv('/app/predictions.csv', index=False)

print('Predictions saved to /app/predictions.csv')
EOF

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingClassifier

# Load data
train = pd.read_csv('/app/data/train.csv')
val = pd.read_csv('/app/data/val.csv')
test = pd.read_csv('/app/data/test.csv')

# Identify columns
num_cols = [c for c in train.columns if c.startswith('num_')]
bin_cols = [c for c in train.columns if c.startswith('bin_')]
cat_cols = [c for c in train.columns if c.startswith('cat_')]

# Target
y_train = train['target']
y_val = val['target']

# Features
X_train = train[num_cols + bin_cols + cat_cols]
X_val = val[num_cols + bin_cols + cat_cols]
X_test = test[num_cols + bin_cols + cat_cols]

# HistGradientBoostingClassifier handles NaNs automatically.
# For categorical features, we can either use the 'categorical_features' parameter
# or simply let it treat them as numeric if they are already encoded as integers.
# Looking at the head of the data, the categorical columns seem to be integers.

# Determine which columns are categorical for the classifier
cat_indices = [X_train.columns.get_loc(col) for col in cat_cols]

# Initialize and train HistGradientBoostingClassifier
model = HistGradientBoostingClassifier(
    max_iter=100,
    learning_rate=0.1,
    max_depth=10,
    categorical_features=cat_indices,
    random_state=42
)

model.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Predict probabilities for the positive class
y_pred = model.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]

# Save predictions to CSV
pred_df = pd.DataFrame({'target': y_pred})
pred_df.to_csv('/app/predictions.csv', index=False)

print('Predictions saved to /app/predictions.csv')
EOF
